budget_items.what_was_said: The Lunenburg Community Food Pantry thanked the board for a cash and grocery gift card donation.
A board member reported the town granted a number of abatements this cycle and gave back an amount to residents; he plans to push a new outreach effort on tax relief and elevator funding programs.
The director said it has been hard to determine exactly how much money is available in the relevant town funds due to staff turnover, and they are working with a vendor to lower upholstery costs.
A representative from We Care 365, a program that pays caregivers to stay home and care for loved ones, is available on-site and will host a breakfast presentation.
The bus for this trip is being paid in part by the Lunenburg Cultural Council.

The board asked whether HR is drafting a job description for a possible combined assistant director/outreach coordinator role, still undecided, with a posted outreach coordinator opening pending applicant review.

decisions.decision: The director has already spoken with the district superintendent, who is interested in developing an intergenerational program pairing seniors with elementary students.
Rather than a formal vote (not on the agenda), board members individually voiced support, as individuals rather than as a body, for further investigating a senior-school partnership program.
General consensus to investigate ways to relieve staff of minute-taking duties, including AI transcription tools and rotating or volunteer note-takers, ahead of the next meeting.
Staff will check with HR on the status of the assistant director job description and try to have an update by the next meeting.

The Council on Aging bylaw language will be brought to the bylaw review committee for research into other towns' bylaws and a rewrite, since it appears outdated and possibly inconsistent with the town-manager form of government.

minutes.headline: COA informally backs pairing seniors with students in schools; board takes over minute-taking to ease staff load
minutes.summary: The Council on Aging discussed a proposed intergenerational program pairing seniors with elementary students to help address school staffing and achievement concerns, which the superintendent is reportedly open to; no formal vote was taken since it wasn't on the agenda, but members voiced individual support. The board also voted to take over producing its own meeting minutes (via AI transcription or volunteers) to reduce strain on short-staffed Senior Center personnel, approved prior minutes, and heard updates on personnel hiring, the 41A elderly tax relief effort, lobby furnishings, an outdated bylaw needing rework, and a full slate of upcoming senior programs and trips.

what_happened.line: Board members individually voiced support for pairing seniors with elementary students, but took no formal vote since the item was not on the agenda.
The board voted to take over producing its own meeting minutes, using AI transcription or volunteers, to ease strain on short-staffed Senior Center personnel.
The Senior Center director reported the district superintendent has expressed interest in developing an intergenerational senior-school program.
Staff will check with HR on the status of an assistant director job description ahead of the next meeting.
The board's own bylaw will go to the bylaw review committee for a rewrite, as it appears outdated and possibly inconsistent with the town-manager form of government.

why_it_matters: A senior-school pairing program would touch both school staffing and student achievement, but it has not been formally proposed, voted on, or agendized by either body.
How the Council on Aging documents its own meetings is changing, which affects public access to the board's record going forward.
A bylaw rewrite could change how the Council on Aging is structured and how it relates to the town-manager form of government.
